en: Selective history attention and distributed state
methods_en: Round 2 used 12 binary events across three channels, querying the latest value of one channel. Three architectures each used three seeds. Interventions flipped relevant, obsolete same-channel or other-channel values, or swapped the last two differing relevant events, with a bag baseline. Round 3 separately trained three two-layer, 16-dimensional, two-head Transformers on three modular-arithmetic evidence pairs, transplanted local or full-layer state, and trained direct-answer MLP/set controls.
results_en: Relevant/obsolete/other TV was 0.9969/0.0011/0.0010 for GRU, 0.9824/0.0047/0.0061 for SSM and 0.9990/0.0003/0.0001 for Transformer. All sequence models correctly flipped after order swaps; the bag model achieved approximately 71.1% ordinarily and 50% averaged over pairs. Top attention located the relevant record in 90.61%, versus 100% for top intervention effect; high-attention/low-effect rate was 16.17%. Round 3 query-only/evidence-only/full-layer donor-rule accuracy was 22.75/37.58/99.33%, with TV 0.7654/0.6120/7.43×10⁻⁹.
interpretation_en: Historical influence measures the output change caused by a value flip. Attention and intervention produce different rankings of that influence. Full-layer copying supplies sufficient state for deterministic downstream computation; the local transfers show how its effect is distributed. Separately trained one-shot MLPs achieved 100% on unseen evidence-x patterns across three seeds. An eight-evidence, 30%-corruption set model averaged 97.17% versus a 97.64% reference, supporting single-forward-pass rule processing.
